question: What would a TV ad campaign for Punctual Pros look like?
html:
Punctual Pros TV campaign

It would be zip-targeted connected TV (CTV), not broadcast. The ads would sell the on-time promise the three franchise brands already make, and success would be measured by booked jobs against holdout zips, not by views (Punctual Pros ad plan).

Why CTV, not broadcast

  • Self-serve CTV now has minimums of $50 to $500 and CPMs of roughly $15 to $40 with zip targeting (Punctual Pros ad plan).
  • That lets a portfolio company of about $22M in revenue buy TV in its roughly 240 zips. It avoids paying for the whole Harrisburg or Philadelphia DMA (Punctual Pros ad plan).
  • Candidate buying tools are Vibe, Disney Campaign Manager, Universal Ads and YouTube on TV screens. Vibe quotes $15 to $35 CPMs and offers zip, household and retargeting options (Punctual Pros ad plan).

Creative

  • Sell existing claims rather than inventing new ones (Punctual Pros ad plan):
  • One Hour: "Always On Time... Or You Don't Pay A Dime!"
  • Ben Franklin: the $5-a-minute guarantee
  • Mister Sparky: "America's On-Time Electrician"
  • First test: "Storm Ready" (:15) against "We Watch the Clock" (:30, cut to :15). Spots are split 50/50 by zip cluster.
  • Specs: 15- or 30-second spots, 1920x1080 preferred, loudness at -24 LKFS ±2 dB.

Role and measurement

  • TV's job is to make the brand familiar before the furnace fails. It should also lift branded search and conversion on Google Local Services Ads, which stay as the always-on base (Punctual Pros ad plan).
  • Judge TV on cost per booked job and geo-holdout lift. Completion rate runs about 94–99% by construction, so it says little (Punctual Pros ad plan).
  • Hold out 15% of Tier-I zips. Cap frequency at 3 per week.

Test sequence

WeekTV step
1Tracking numbers, QR codes, site pixel, holdout zips set
2Creative A/B launch
3Frequency check
4Read booked jobs per 10k households, exposed vs holdout; shift 20% of budget to the winning cut
5Weather-trigger pacing in alternating counties
6Vendor split: Vibe vs Disney Campaign Manager or YouTube TV screens

Weekly test budgets are $8,000 in week 1 and $12,500 in weeks 2–5. Those figures cover all channels, so the plan's excerpt does not show a TV-only spend (Punctual Pros ad plan).

Open gaps

  • The $12 cost per site visit is an assumption drawn from direct-to-consumer case studies. No home-services CTV benchmark was found, and the week-8 read must replace it (Punctual Pros ad plan).
  • A TV-only budget and a target cost per booked job are not in the context. Both would come from the full channel allocation and ServiceTitan job-margin data.

Next actions

  • Set the TV-only share of the weekly test budget and a target cost per booked job, using ServiceTitan margin data.
  • Lock the holdout zip list and tracking numbers before any spot runs.
  • Produce both :15 cuts to spec and confirm brand-claim approval with the franchisor.
  • Schedule the week-4 and week-8 reads. Replace the est. $12 cost per visit with observed data.
